title: Battle for the Body: an AI-assisted biology RTS, with a free browser demo
author: yko-20
selftext:
I have released Battle for the Body, a real-time strategy game set inside the human body. Generative AI assisted with the code, graphics, sounds, and text. The game runs as an HTML file in a desktop browser.



There are three factions with different mechanics: the Immune System builds and adapts, Bacteria multiply and use quorum signaling, and Viruses & Prions hijack host cells. Biology provides the inspiration, while scale, timing, and combat are simplified for play.



One recent part of the AI workflow was making new artwork for the [itch.io](http://itch.io) page instead of reusing the main-screen image everywhere. I tried a generated background and banner, then kept the banner and switched the page background back to a solid dark color. The simpler background looked better around the game and text. That small iteration has me thinking about how much visual detail helps a strategy game, and when it just gets in the way.



For others using generated art in strategy games, how do you keep units and factions easy to read while still giving them distinct visual identities? Feedback on tutorial clarity and the three factions is welcome too.



Free browser tutorial and game page: [https://yko79135.itch.io/battle-for-the-body](https://yko79135.itch.io/battle-for-the-body)



Free full matches as the Immune System: [https://yko79135.itch.io/battle-for-the-body-free-demo](https://yko79135.itch.io/battle-for-the-body-free-demo)



The full download is US$4.99, with all three factions and four body environments.
